title: Development of an AI-assisted detection system for gastric cancer and precancerous lesions in the upper gastrointestinal tract
summary:
Gastric cancer is often detected only at an advanced stage. Early forms of gastric cancer and changes that may develop into cancer can also be easily missed during an examination of the stomach. At the same time, these examinations generate large numbers of images and videos, and their interpretation depends on the experience of the examiner and on the quality of the examination. Modern computer-based methods may help to identify suspicious changes more reliably and to improve examination quality.

The aim of this study is to investigate whether a computer-based system can help detect and classify gastric cancer and possible precancerous changes on images and videos obtained during stomach examinations. In addition, the study will assess whether such a system can help determine whether all important areas of the stomach were adequately examined.

The study will analyze existing and newly collected image and video data from routine clinical care. These data come from adult patients with gastric cancer or corresponding precancerous changes for whom a confirmed tissue-based diagnosis is available. The data will be processed without direct personal identifiers. Based on these data, the computer-based system will be developed, trained, and evaluated. The study will then assess how well the system identifies suspicious changes, how reliably it distinguishes abnormal from normal tissue, and whether it can assess the quality of the examination. No additional examination or treatment will be performed as part of the study.
conditions: Helicobacter pylori [H.pylori] as the cause of diseases classified to other chapters

interventions.name: Included are adult patients with gastric carcinoma or precancerous gastric lesions for whom endoscopic image and/or video data from routine clinical diagnostics as well as a corresponding histopathological reference standard are available. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Age ≥ 18 years
2. Gastric cancer or precancerous gastric lesion
3. Availability of endoscopic image and/or video data
4. Availability of a corresponding histopathological reference standard
5. Sufficient image/video quality for algorithmic analysis
6. In gastric cancer cases: histology from endoscopic resection or surgical specimen
7. In surgically treated cases: endoscopic imaging obtained no more than 30 days before surgery
8. Data derived from the period
Exclusion criteria:
1. Age < 18 years
2. Missing endoscopic image and/or video data
3. Missing corresponding histopathological reference standard
4. Insufficient image or video quality for algorithmic analysis
5. In gastric cancer cases: biopsy-only confirmed cases without resection or surgical histology
6. Surgically treated gastric cancer cases if the corresponding endoscopic imaging was obtained more than 30 days before surgery
7. Missing or insufficient linkage between endoscopic data and histopathological findings
8. Presence of direct personal identifiers in the datasets to be analyzed if anonymization or pseudonymization for study use is not possible
